newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Yachting: Peter Campbell's Rhumbline Column.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Yachting: Peter Campbell's Rhumbline Column.

text.p: By Peter Campbell*
OLYMPIC CLASSES ON SYDNEY HARBOUR
Nine of the 10 Olympic sailing classes for the Sydney 2000 Games, including a regatta debut by the Australian-designed 49er, will be competing in Sail Sydney '97 on Sydney Harbour over Easter.

Sail Sydney is the premier Olympic and International Youth classes regatta sailed annually on the harbour and will play an important role in Olympic preparations for Australian and international competitors over the next four years.
Organised by the Yachting Association of New South Wales, the sailing will be over the new Olympic courses.
Various classes being hosted by the Royal Sydney Yacht Squadron (49er), Middle Harbour Yacht Club (Tornado, Soling and 470) and Woollahra Sailing Club (Laser, Laser Radial, Finn, Europe and 420).

Racing will begin on Good Friday March 28 and continue through to Easter Monday with highlights being the regatta debut by the Bethwaite-designed 49er attracting many of Australia's best skiff sailors, including 18-footer champion CHRIS NICHOLSON, and the revival of competition in the Solings, the only keelboat in the Sydney 2000 regatta.
BOOTH & BEASHEL RISE IN RANKINGS

Olympic silver medallist MITCH BOOTH and ADAM BEASHEL, his new crew in the Tornado catamaran class, have moved up to fourth in the world Tornado rankings, according to the International Sailing Federation (ISAF).
This follows their overall win at Sail Auckland and second overall at Sail Melbourne so far this year, with only crews from Germany, Spain and Austria ahead of them in the rankings.

BEASHEL, younger brother of COLIN BEASHEL, the Olympic Star class bronze medallist at Savannah, is better known as an America's Cup and a Laser sailor but has adapted exceptionally well to the high performance tactical sailing of the Tornado class.

MATT HAYES, who sailed well in the Soling class at Savannah, maintains his fifth place in world rankings behind Swedish, Danish, Spain and Norwegian crews, while Australian NATASHA STURGES is also fifth in the Mistral women's sailboards.
Other Australians ranked in the top 20 by the ISAF are BRENDON TODD (10) and LARS KLEPPICH (19) in Mistral men's sailboards, PAUL McKENZIE (18) in Finns and MICHAEL BLACKBURN (eighth) in Lasers.

Holding number one ranking in the Mistral women is LAI SHAN LEE who, at Savannah, became Hong Kong's firstever gold medal. Currently studying at the Australian National University, she won the Mistrals at both Sail Melbourne and Sail Auckland to maintain her international status.
INTERNATIONAL SUCCESS FOR DESIGN GROUP

Its not just our sailors who are doing well on the international boating scene. The Miami Boat Show, one of America's largest displays of boats and boating equipment, has been a happy hunting ground for Australian design group, Crowther Multihulls.
Managing director BRETT CROWTHER has returned to Sydney from Miami confident his company's designs continue to be among the world's best.

As well as being a guest speaker at the international multihull yacht designer's forum at the show, CROWTHER saw the Crowther-designed 57-foot sail game fishing catamaran become a star attraction among the many multihulls yachts on display.
This was the second of the design to be built. The original yacht has already cruised more than 36,000 nautical miles in the Pacific and brought home plenty of fish.

The impact of the yacht was such that the builders, Alwoplast from Chile, left the show with two confirmed orders for 50ft luxury power catamarans which will be created to a special design from Crowthers.
Even more impressive was the release of the Crowther 45 flybridge motor-sailer which will also be built by Alwoplast with four confirmed orders for the new design and several more pending.
QUEST TO MAKE MOOLOOLABA
Cruising Yacht Club member BOB STEEL will be back into ocean racing with his well-performed Nelson/Marek 43, Quest, in the 34th Sydney-Mooloolaba race which starts Saturday March 22.
Quest was an early casualty of the southerly buster which hit the fleet only a matter of hours after the start last year's Telstra Sydney-Hobart, twisting her mast out of shape.

A new rig has finally arrived for the boat which, along with SYD FISCHER's Ragamuffin and Ausmaid, owned by Melbourne yachtsman GIORGIO GJERGJA, was a member of the winning Australian team at the 1996 Kenwood Cup in Hawaii.

Quest and Ragamuffin, along with RAY ROBERTS' Corel 45, BZW Challenge, WARWICK MILLER's Reichel/Pugh 66, Exile, and STEVE KULMAR's Mumm 36, Sea, are favourites for the top IMS racer honours in Middle Harbour Yacht Club's annual autumn classic.
However, one to watch in her first long ocean race will be the IAIN MURRAY designed 36-footer Bashfull, with CYCA Vice-Commodore HUGO VAN KRETSCHMAR on the helm.

The Sydney eastern suburbs property developer and son-in-law of the late JACK ROOKLYN, has won eight of 15 short offshore national and club races with the Bashford International-built sloop, including four races in the inaugural Telstra Cup regatta.
"I'd like to win in memory of JACK, who made such a contribution to the Mooloolaba race, taking line honours seven times, a record six times with his maxi Apollo," VAN KRETSCHMAR said this week.
SYD FISCHER CELEBRATES SEVENTY

SYD FISCHER, arguably Australia's most successful ocean racing yachtsman, celebrated his 70th birthday last weekend, but has no plans to ease back in his sailing or business interests, which include owning and operating the Gazebo Hotel.

The former Australian Yachtsman of the Year and Ocean Racing Yachtsman of the Year for 1996 will skipper his Farr 50 Ragamuffin in next weekend's race to Mooloolaba and is also keeping a close eye on the building of a new Farr 50 which he will sail in the Admiral's Cup in England in July/August.

FISCHER will announce his crew for the Admiral's Cup following the Mooloolaba race which he described as an important part of crew training, with its tricky winds and currents over a coastal passage course.
However, FISCHER has already nominated Olympian MATT HAYES as the principal helmsman and sailmaker MICHAEL COXON as tactician.
SAILABILITY WEEKEND PLANNED

Among the fleet of near 50 yachts heading for Mooloolaba next weekend will be DAVID PESCUD's Aspect Computing, again with a crew of sailors with disabilities, continuing the remarkably successful project which has included competing in races to Lord Howe Island and Hobart.

Boating and sailing are among the few active sports which can be enjoyed by people of all ages and with all forms and levels of disabilities -- physical, intellectual, sensory, learning or psychiatric -- although not everyone can cope with the rigours of ocean racing.

Leading a campaign to enable more people with disabilities to enjoy boating and sailing as a recreation and in competition is Sailability, a national non-profit organisation chaired by KAY COTTEE, the first woman to sail around the world, alone and nonstop.

Appropriately, as the crew of Aspect Computing set sail for Mooloolaba, yacht and sailing clubs throughout Australia will be taking part in a national fundraising campaign by Sailability. Everyone who goes out on the water over that weekend will be asked to donate A$2 to Sailability.
Our primary aim is to increase the number of active disabled sailors throughout the country, COTTEE said. But we also aim to have a competitive Australian sailing team at the 2000 Paralympics.
*Peter Campbell is editor of Offshore Yachting magazine. * Peter Campbell is editor of OFFSHORE Yachting magazine.
